prompt.en: A parts list needs 0.82 A. A meter on the same accessory reads 820 mA. What should the learner conclude?

text.en: The readings differ by a factor of ten.

feedback.en: That would follow from dividing by 100. Milli requires dividing by 1 000.
820 / 1 000 = 0.82 A, so only the display unit differs.

text.en: The meter reads a thousand times too high.

feedback.en: 820 is a larger number because mA is a smaller unit. The current itself is unchanged.

text.en: The readings differ by a factor of one hundred.

feedback.en: This treats milli as a tenfold step. It is a thousandth of an ampere.

explanation.en: Compare values only after expressing them in the same unit.

prompt.en: A cable has sound copper conductors, but its plastic separator cracks and lets them touch. Which change explains the fault?

text.en: The copper now has the resistance of an insulator.

feedback.en: The copper is still conductive. The failed separation creates the unwanted path.

text.en: The return conductor has stopped carrying charge because plastic supplies it.

feedback.en: Plastic normally separates the conductors; it does not supply their current.

text.en: An insulating barrier has failed, allowing an unintended conductive path.

feedback.en: The separator keeps the intended paths apart. Contact between conductors can create a short.

text.en: The plastic has become a normal series resistor in the intended path.

feedback.en: The described fault is conductor contact, not a resistor deliberately inserted in series.

explanation.en: Materials have different jobs: conductors carry current, and insulation keeps those paths separate.

prompt.en: A DC accessory has equal-sized red and black leads. Which check matters before connecting a replacement supply?

text.en: Confirm the required positive and negative connections in its instructions.

feedback.en: Equal wire size does not remove polarity requirements. Verify the specified connections.

text.en: Choose polarity from which wire has the lower resistance.

feedback.en: Wire resistance does not establish the required input polarity.

text.en: Swap the leads if the supply has a lower current rating.

feedback.en: Current capacity and polarity are separate. Swapping leads does not correct a rating mismatch.

text.en: Use either orientation if the two leads have equal length.

feedback.en: Lead length does not make a polarity-sensitive circuit reversible.

explanation.en: A DC circuit can depend on current direction even when both supply leads look alike.
